formulation.rationale: Both mapped products are insulin detemir, with one concentration-unspecified entry and one Levemir U-100 entry. The compared society guidance names detemir or long-acting basal insulin analogues and does not provide a brand- or U-100-specific fasting instruction.

passages.page: not exposed in HTML; article pp. 16-38
passages.quote: All patients receiving insulin before admission require insulin during the perioperative period (112, 113). For most patients, this requirement includes administration of a percentage of the usual basal insulin (NPH, detemir, glargine) in combination with correction doses of regular insulin or rapid-acting insulin analogs for glucose levels from 8.3 to 11.1 mmol/liter (150 to 200 mg/dl).

passages.page: not exposed in HTML; article pp. 16-38
passages.quote: Because the pharmacokinetic properties of NPH insulin differ from those of glargine and detemir, dose reductions of 25–50% are suggested, together with the administration of short- or rapid-acting insulin for BG > 8.3 mmol/liter (150 mg/dl) (Table 3).

passages.page: not exposed in HTML; article pp. 16-38
passages.quote: We recommend that all patients with type 1 diabetes who undergo minor or major surgical procedures receive either CII or sc basal insulin with bolus insulin as required to prevent hyperglycemia during the perioperative period. (1|⊕⊕⊕⊕)

passages.page: not exposed in HTML; article pp. 16-38
passages.quote: When instituting sc insulin therapy in the postsurgical setting, we recommend that basal (for patients who are NPO) or basal bolus (for patients who are eating) insulin therapy be instituted as the preferred approach. (1|⊕⊕⊕○)

comparisons.checked_locators: 5.3 Perioperative BG control, Recommendations 5.3.1-5.3.3 and evidence
comparisons.note: The Endocrine Society guideline explicitly names detemir in perioperative basal-insulin management, suggests a 25–50% dose reduction for glargine/detemir, and recommends basal insulin through the perioperative and postsurgical periods.

comparisons.checked_locators: Perioperative Care; Insulin Therapy Recommendations 16.8 and 16.9
comparisons.note: ADA provides a current long-acting basal-insulin adjustment before surgery and retains basal insulin in NPO/poor-intake and adequate-intake regimens.

comparisons.checked_locators: Recommendations Before Colonoscopy > Patient Education and Navigation
comparisons.note: USMSTF states that antihyperglycemic management around colonoscopy should be individualized with the prescribing clinician and does not provide a detemir-specific dose.

recommendations.timing_text: On the evening before surgery, reduce long-acting basal insulin analogs to 75–80% of the usual dose
recommendations.strength: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.certainty: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.applicability: Long-acting basal insulin analogue use before surgery, including insulin detemir.
recommendations.exceptions: ADA states that adjustment depends on diabetes type and clinical judgment.
recommendations.summary: ADA recommends 75–80% of the usual long-acting basal-insulin dose on the evening before surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Noncritically ill patient with poor oral intake or taking nothing by mouth.
recommendations.exceptions: This establishes continuation of a basal component but does not specify a detemir dose.
recommendations.summary: ADA retains basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan during poor oral intake or NPO status.

recommendations.timing_text: receive either CII or sc basal insulin with bolus insulin as required
recommendations.applicability: Patient with type 1 diabetes undergoing a minor or major procedure.
recommendations.exceptions: The recommendation allows either continuous insulin infusion or subcutaneous basal insulin with bolus insulin as required.
recommendations.summary: For type 1 diabetes, the Endocrine Society recommends continued insulin coverage with CII or subcutaneous basal insulin during the perioperative period.

recommendations.exceptions: No fixed detemir restart time or patient-specific dose is stated.
recommendations.summary: The Endocrine Society recommends basal insulin as the preferred postsurgical approach for patients who remain NPO.

recommendations.timing_text: basal bolus (for patients who are eating)
recommendations.exceptions: No fixed detemir restart time or patient-specific dose is stated.
recommendations.summary: The Endocrine Society recommends a basal-bolus insulin approach after surgery when the patient is eating.

scenario_coverage.reason: Endocrine Society provides detemir-specific dose-reduction guidance and ADA provides a current long-acting basal-insulin adjustment.
ADA retains basal insulin during NPO/poor intake; Endocrine Society explicitly requires basal insulin coverage for type 1 diabetes.
Endocrine Society provides postsurgical basal or basal-bolus guidance based on whether the patient remains NPO or is eating.

conflicts.description: The Endocrine Society suggests a 25–50% reduction for glargine/detemir, whereas ADA 2026 recommends reducing long-acting basal insulin analogues to 75–80% of the usual dose on the evening before surgery. These numeric frameworks are preserved separately.

open_questions.text: USMSTF does not provide a colonoscopy-specific insulin detemir dose and explicitly directs individualized antihyperglycemic medication management with the prescribing clinician.
The compared society sources do not identify a separate perioperative fasting instruction for Levemir U-100 versus concentration-unspecified insulin detemir.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package. The ADA and Endocrine Society preprocedure dose frameworks are not numerically identical and are intentionally preserved as a conflict. No patient-specific insulin dose is calculated.
